info.title: Anjung API
info.summary: Anjung: multi-tenant rental management for Malaysia.
info.description:
REST API served by the FastAPI `api` service behind an ALB.

**Authentication.** Cognito access token (Authorization Code + PKCE) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The organisation, roles and tenant ID come only from validated token claims (`org_id`, `roles`, `tenant_id`). They are never accepted from the request body, path or query.

**Tenancy.** Every resource is scoped to the caller's organisation. Identifiers from other organisations behave as if they do not exist (404).

**Money.** Integer minor units (sen) plus currency. Never floats.

**Pagination.** `limit` and `cursor`. Cursors are opaque and HMAC-signed.

**Idempotency.** `Idempotency-Key` header is required on money-creating POSTs.

**Errors.** Consistent `Error` envelope with `code`, `message`, `details` and `request_id`. `400 bad_request` means the request could not be parsed (malformed JSON, invalid cursor). `422 validation_error` means it parsed but failed validation, with per-field `details`. `409` covers state conflicts, including domain codes such as `lease_overlap`.

**Platform scope.** Endpoints under `/v1/platform` are the only ones that take an organisation ID as input. They require the `platform_admin` role and every call is audited with a reason.

**Changes in 0.2.0.** Renamed to Anjung. Added platform organisation endpoints. Late-fee percentage is now integer basis points (`percent_bp`). `lease_overlap` returns 409 instead of 422. Shared `422 ValidationFailed` response added to every operation that accepts input. `fake` provider key added for dev and staging smoke tests.

**Changes in 0.2.1.** `vendor` role reserved and not grantable in v1. QR creation documented as on-demand with provider-defined, possibly short, validity.

**Changes in 0.3.0 (breaking).** Room-by-room letting: `Unit.type`, `parent_unit_id` and `letting_mode`; `room` removed from `Property.type`. Leases may be rolling (`end_date` null) with `notice_days`. `deposit` replaced by `deposits` (by type). New `POST /v1/leases/{lease_id}/charges` for one-off charges. Maintenance requests can target shared areas (`area`, `property_id`).

**Changes in 0.3.2.** Read-only display fields, all optional: `Lease.property_name`, `unit_label`, `parent_unit_label` and `tenants` (id and name), and `Tenant.rentals` (current and upcoming leases with their unit or room).

**Changes in 0.4.0 (breaking for property managers).** Manager scope: a `property_manager` (without `org_admin`) sees only the properties they manage (`Property.manager_id`: the creator, reassignable by an org admin through `PATCH /v1/properties/{property_id}`) and what hangs off them: units, leases, invoices, ledgers, maintenance requests, documents, reports and notification log entries. They see the tenants they created plus every tenant on a lease in one of their properties. Anything else answers 404, like another organisation's data. Unmatched payments, their allocation and invoice runs are org-wide and now `org_admin` only. Org admins and tenants are unaffected.

**Changes in 0.5.0.** Staff access window: `User.active_from` / `active_until` (set on invite or `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}`) and the computed `User.access`. A staff member who is disabled or outside their dates gets `403 account_inactive` at sign-in and on every request, so it applies at once; reactivating (status `active` and/or new dates) restores everything. Nothing they managed is removed.

**Changes in 0.6.0.** Property limit per property manager: `User.property_quota` (set on invite or `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}`, null = no limit) and `User.properties_managed`. Active properties count; archived ones do not. Creating a property, or an admin assigning one, beyond the limit is `409 quota_exceeded`. `PropertyPage.quota` shows a manager their usage. Org admins are never limited. `Me.active_from` / `active_until` let staff see their own access dates. `MaintenanceRequest` gains display names: `property_name`, `unit_label`, `parent_unit_label`, `reported_by_name`, `assigned_to_name`. `Tenant.tenancy` says whether a tenant rents now (current, upcoming, past, none), apart from their account status.

**Changes in 0.7.0.** Tenancy agreement signing: `POST /v1/leases/{lease_id}/agreement/send`, `/sign` (tenant) and `/paper`, and `Lease.agreement`. With `OrgSettings.require_signed_agreement` (default on) a lease activates only after every tenant has signed. A tenant sees a draft lease once its agreement is sent. Changing a draft's terms after sending clears the signatures. Dates in human-readable messages (and receipts) are shown as DD-MM-YYYY; API fields stay ISO 8601.

**Changes in 0.7.1.** `LeaseUpdate.deposits`: a draft lease's deposits can be changed before activation (422 once active). A change clears agreement signatures, like the other terms.

**Changes in 0.8.0.** Set-password links for tenants. `POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/invite` takes an optional body `{channel}`: `email` (default, Cognito's invitation email with a temporary password, as before), `whatsapp` (the app sends a one-time set-password link over WhatsApp; needs the tenant's number and recorded WhatsApp consent) or `link` (the link is returned for staff to share, for example from their own WhatsApp). It now returns `TenantInviteResult`. New public endpoints `GET /v1/invites/{token}` and `POST /v1/invites/{token}/accept` show the invitation and set the password. A link works once, only the newest link works, and it expires with the invitation (7 days). Unknown, used, replaced and expired links all answer 404.

**Changes in 0.9.0 (breaking for property archiving).** One lifecycle in every module: deactivate, reactivate, delete. Properties and units: status `archived` is now `inactive` (`archived` is still accepted as input until 0.11). New `POST /v1/properties/{property_id}/deactivate` and `/reactivate`, and the same for units; units switched off with their property or unit come back with it. `DELETE /v1/properties/{property_id}` now **deletes** (it used to archive) and needs a `reason`. Every delete has a preview, `GET …/deletion`, returning `DeletionPreview` (`mode`: `remove`, `erase` or `blocked`, with blockers and what it affects). New deletes: units and rooms, tenants, draft leases, closed or cancelled maintenance requests (org admin). Something that never had a lease is removed completely; a tenant with lease history is erased (anonymised, through a privacy request; org admin only); lease history, open money and live leases block. Records with history are deleted by the retention purge job once the retention period (decision D5) has passed; it is off until then.

**Changes in 0.10.0.** Parking bays. `Unit.type` gains `parking`. A bay sits at property level and may be allocated to a whole unit (`parent_unit_id`): while that unit is let as a whole the bay comes with it (`Lease.included_bays`) and cannot be let separately (422 on create, 409 on activation); when the unit is let by the room, or for a property bay, the bay is let on its own lease. Bay labels are unique per property, apart from unit labels. `UnitUpdate.parent_unit_id` re-allocates a bay (null makes it a property bay); refused while the bay has a live, upcoming or draft lease. Switching a unit back to letting as a whole is refused while one of its bays is let separately. Deleting a whole unit keeps its bays as property bays. `Unit.note` (e.g. level, covered). `Lease.vehicle_plate` (bay leases only; personal data: exported, and removed on erasure). Display fields `Lease.unit_type`, `TenantRental.unit_type`. The occupancy report counts separately let bays in `bays_total` and `bays_occupied`, outside `units_total` and the rate. The `archived` status alias stays accepted until 0.11.

**Changes in 0.11.0.** Organisation branding (each company is its own organisation). `Organization.branding` and `OrganizationUpdate.branding` (a partial update; org admin): `enabled`, `handle` (unique across the platform, 3 to 30 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; some words reserved), `display_name`, `company_name`, `company_reg_no`, `accent_colour`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `welcome_text` (en, ms), `login_page`, and `logo_document_id` (a clean `logo` document owned by the organisation: PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 512 KB). A changed handle keeps working for 30 days. `OrganizationCreate.branding` lets the platform admin set it at creation. New public `GET /v1/brands/{handle}` (`PublicBrand`, for the sign-in page at `/login/<handle>`) and `GET /v1/brands/{handle}/logo`; unknown, disabled and inactive brands answer 404. `Me.branding` and `InviteInfo.brand` carry the public brand when branding is on. Documents gain owner type `organization` and type `logo` (org admin only). With branding on, emails show the logo, name and company details and come from "<brand> via Anjung" with the contact email as reply-to; receipts show the company name, registration number and logo.

**Changes in 0.12.0.** A company's plan, set by the platform admin: `Organization.plan` (`property_limit`, `active_until`, `properties_used`, `status`, `read_only_until`), `OrganizationCreate.plan`, and `PATCH /v1/platform/organizations/{org_id}/plan` (with a reason, audited). Within its limit (units since 0.13.0), the org admin still divides the plan up: managers' limits cannot add up to more than the organisation's limit, and staff `active_until` cannot be later than the organisation's (422). After `active_until` the organisation is read-only for staff for 30 days: writes answer `403 plan_read_only`, except recording money received and privacy requests; tenants are unaffected. After that nobody in the organisation can sign in or use the API (`403 plan_ended`). `Me.plan` gives staff their organisation's plan. Org admins are emailed 30, 7 and 1 day before the end date.

**Changes in 0.13.0 (breaking for limits).** Limits count **units**, not properties, so neither a big building nor many properties gets round them: every whole unit that is on, in a property that is on. Rooms, parking bays and empty properties are free. The plan's `property_limit` / `properties_used` become `unit_limit` / `units_used`; a manager's `property_quota` / `properties_managed` become `unit_quota` / `units_managed`, and `PropertyPage.quota` counts units. The limit is checked when a whole unit is added or reactivated, when a property comes back with its units, and when a property moves to a manager (for that manager). Creating an empty property is never refused. Values stored under the old names are read as the new ones.

**Changes in 0.13.1.** `Error.params`: the values in the message, so clients can show it in the user's language. Sent with `quota_exceeded` and `plan_read_only`.

**Changes in 0.13.2.** `Property.units_active`: the whole units that are on, which is what the plan and manager limits count. `unit_count` also includes units that are off. Sent by `createProperty`, `getProperty` and `listProperties`.

**Changes in 0.14.0.** `POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/invite` with `channel: email` (the default) sends the app's own welcome email with a one-time set-password link, branded like the other emails, instead of Cognito's invitation email with a temporary password. The response shape is unchanged; `link` stays null. A tenant who was sent a temporary password before can be invited again to get a link.

**Changes in 0.15.0.** Staff welcome emails: inviting a staff member (`inviteUser`) and creating an organisation (its first admin) send the app's own welcome email with a one-time set-password link (`/invite/<token>`, the same link and endpoints as tenants), branded like the other emails, instead of Cognito's invitation with a temporary password; without email sending set up, Cognito's email is used as before. `InviteInfo.kind` (`tenant` or `staff`). New `POST /v1/users/{user_id}/invite` (`resendUserInvite`, org admin) and `POST /v1/platform/organizations/{org_id}/admin-invite` (`resendOrganizationAdminInvite`, with a reason) send a fresh link to staff who have not signed in yet; the previous link stops working. Welcome emails (tenant or staff) are not sent to an address on the bounce/complaint list: `409 address_suppressed`, with `params.scope` `tenant` or `staff`. Reports: new `GET /v1/reports/maintenance` (`getMaintenanceReport`: per property, open requests now, how urgent and how old, and those resolved in the period with the average days to resolve), and `format=csv` on every report returns the same rows as a CSV download (`text/csv`, UTF-8 with BOM, with property, unit and tenant names).

**Changes in 0.16.0.** Messages in the user's language, for the rest of the errors. Each item of `Error.details` now has a `code` (machine-readable: the validator's error type such as `missing` or `string_too_short`, or a code made from the fixed English `issue`, such as `must_not_be_before_from`) and, where the issue has values in it, `params` (for example `min_length`, `max_length`, `ge`, `days`, `date`). `Blocker.params` carries the values in a delete blocker's message (`amount_minor`, `count`, `what`, `units`, `more`). `issue` and `message` stay the English fallback.

**Changes in 0.17.0.** The platform admin can correct a company's details: `PATCH /v1/platform/organizations/{org_id}/details` (`updateOrganizationDetails`) changes the name and the branding (handle, names, registration number, colour, contacts, welcome text, sign-in page), with a reason. Same rules as the org admin's `updateOrganization` (a handle another company uses is 409); audited in both organisations as `org.update`. Settings and the logo stay with the org admin.

post.description: Writes the organisation, its REGISTRY#ORG entry and the first membership in one transaction, then sends the invitation. Since 0.15.0 the first admin gets the app's welcome email with a one-time set-password link instead of Cognito's invitation (if it cannot be sent, the organisation is still created; use `resendOrganizationAdminInvite`).

post.description: Creates the Cognito user with AdminCreateUser and a membership item. Sends an invitation email. Since 0.15.0 the new staff member gets the app's welcome email with a one-time set-password link (branded when branding is on) instead of Cognito's invitation; if that email cannot be sent the user is still added and the answer is 409 (use `resendUserInvite`).

delete.description: Deletes a property that never had a lease (made by mistake) with its units, rooms and documents. 409 when blocked: lease history (deactivate it instead; the retention purge deletes it later) or maintenance requests. See the preview.

parameters.description: List the rooms of one whole unit.

post.description: Creates a whole unit, or a room inside a whole unit of the same property. Rooms cannot contain rooms.

get.description: Tenants may read only units they currently or previously leased.

patch.description: `type` and `parent_unit_id` cannot change. Changing `letting_mode` fails with 409 invalid_state while any lease on the unit or its rooms is active or future.

delete.description: Deletes a unit (with its rooms) or a room that never had a lease, with its documents. 409 when blocked by lease or maintenance history.

get.description: A tenant may read only their own record.

delete.description: `remove`: deletes the tenant and everything indexed under them (consents, documents, messages, maintenance requests, privacy requests), their invitation and their login. `erase`: org admin only; opens a deletion privacy request and starts anonymisation (`outcome: erasure_started`). 409 when blocked.

post.description: `email` (default): creates the Cognito user without Cognito's own email (first time) and sends the app's welcome email with a one-time set-password link, branded when the organisation's branding is on (0.14.0; before, Cognito's invitation email with a temporary password). 409 when email sending is not set up or the email could not be sent, and `409 address_suppressed` when the address is on the bounce/complaint list (0.15.0). `whatsapp`: the same link sent over WhatsApp (422 without a phone number or WhatsApp consent, 409 when WhatsApp sending is not set up). `link`: the same link, returned in the response for staff to share themselves. The link is never returned for `email` or `whatsapp`, and never stored in the notification log. A new link replaces the previous one. Audited as `tenant.invite` with the channel.

get.summary: Export all data held for a tenant

get.description: Tenants always receive only their own leases, regardless of filters.

post.description: Fails with 409 lease_overlap if the dates overlap another active or future lease on the unit.

delete.description: Deletes a draft lease that never started, with its tenant links, uploaded documents and any agreement signatures. 409 for any other status.

post.description: Takes the unit's lease lock, checks the letting mode (a room needs its parent in `rooms` mode, a whole unit needs `whole`), sets status to active and creates one deposit invoice with a line per deposit. Fails with 409 lease_overlap if another lease on the unit overlaps the dates, or 409 invalid_state if the letting mode does not allow it. When the organisation requires it (`require_signed_agreement`, default on), every tenant must have signed the tenancy agreement first, else 409 invalid_state.
For rolling leases the termination date must be at least `notice_days` after today unless `waive_notice` is true.
Fails with 409 lease_overlap if another lease on the unit overlaps the dates.

Creates an invoice with a single one-off line (for example a share of a utility bill or a repair), adds the ledger charge and notifies the tenant. Allowed on active, terminated and expired leases, so final bills can be raised after move-out.

post.summary: Create or refresh a dynamic DuitNow QR
post.description: Returns the existing unexpired QR for the current outstanding amount if one exists, otherwise creates one. Validity is set by the payment provider and can be as short as about a minute, so clients call this when the payer opens the pay screen, show a countdown, and call again after expiry. QR images are never sent in email or WhatsApp; messages carry a link to the pay screen. The reference follows the provider's rules (prefix `ANJ`). Fails with 409 invalid_state if the invoice is paid or void.

Verifies signature and timestamp on the raw body, enqueues the event, and returns 200 quickly. Processing is asynchronous and idempotent.

A tenant can list only their own tenant record, their own leases and their own maintenance requests and invoices. An owner in another organisation is reported as 404.

post.summary: Send the tenancy agreement for signing
post.description: Draft leases only. Uses a clean `lease_agreement` document on the lease (409 if none). The tenants can then see the draft lease and its documents, and are notified (`lease_agreement_sent`). Sending again starts over: earlier signatures are dropped.

The tenant types their full name and agrees. Recorded with the time, the document and the signing device. When the last tenant signs, the agreement is `signed`. 409 if nothing is waiting or they already signed; 422 if the name does not match.

post.summary: Record that tenants signed on paper
post.description: For tenants who cannot use the portal. The signed scan must be uploaded first as a `lease_agreement` document.

get.description: Public: the link is the credential. Returns who is invited and by which organisation. 404 for unknown, used, replaced or expired links, and when the organisation is not active.

post.summary: Set the password and activate the account
post.description: Public. Sets the tenant's permanent password, links the account (status `active`) and uses up the link. The tenant then signs in as usual. A password that breaks the rules is 422 and the link stays valid. Audited as `tenant.invite_accept`.
Hides the property and its units from new leases and default lists. 409 while a unit has an active, upcoming or draft lease. Idempotent. Reactivate undoes it.
Undoes deactivate. Units switched off with the property come back; units deactivated on their own stay off. The manager's property limit applies (409 quota_exceeded).
A whole unit's rooms are deactivated with it. 409 while it or a room has an active, upcoming or draft lease.
Undoes deactivate; rooms switched off with their unit come back. 409 while the property, or a room's unit, is inactive.

get.summary: Preview deleting a unit or room

get.description: `remove` when the tenant never had a lease; `erase` when they have lease history (org admin only); `blocked` while a lease is draft or active, money is owed either way or deposits are held, or when already erased.
Only a draft can be deleted.
Org admin only. Only closed or cancelled requests can be deleted.
Public: what the sign-in page at `/login/<handle>` shows. Nothing private. 404 for unknown, disabled or inactive brands, and for a changed handle after its 30-day grace. Rate-limited per client IP.
Public image, cacheable (the URL changes with the logo). Served with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Cache key, the logo's document id.

patch.description: Unit limit and end date for the whole organisation. Lowering the limit below what is in use removes nothing; it only stops new units. Audited in both organisations as `org.plan` with the reason.

patch.summary: Correct a company's name and branding
patch.description: The company name and branding (handle, names, registration number, colour, contacts, welcome text, sign-in page). Partial: fields left out stay as they are. The same checks as `updateOrganization`; a handle another company uses, or gave up less than the grace period ago, is 409. The platform organisation is 404 and a closed one 409. Settings and the logo stay with the org admin: `branding.logo_document_id` is refused (422). Audited in both organisations as `org.update` with the reason.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `csv` returns the same rows as a spreadsheet download (0.15.0).

get.description: Per property: requests open now (all statuses before resolved), those with priority high or urgent, and the age in days of the oldest; and the requests resolved in the period (`from`/`to`, months, by `resolved_at`, including ones since closed) with the average days from report to resolution, plus those cancelled in the period. Without `from`/`to`, all time. A property manager sees only their properties. Added in 0.15.0.

post.summary: Send a staff member a new welcome email
post.description: For a staff member who has not signed in yet (409 otherwise): a fresh welcome email with a one-time set-password link; the previous link stops working. Without email sending set up, Cognito's invitation is resent. 409 `address_suppressed` when the address bounced. Audited as `user.invite_resend`. Added in 0.15.0.

post.summary: Send a company's first admin a new welcome email
post.description: Each org admin of the organisation who has not signed in yet gets a fresh welcome email with a one-time set-password link (or Cognito's invitation again when email sending is not set up); their previous link stops working. 409 when every admin has signed in. Audited in both organisations as `user.invite_resend` with the reason. Added in 0.15.0.

webhookSignature.name: X-Signature
webhookSignature.description: HMAC signature over the raw body, plus a timestamp header (provider specific). Verified with the secret in Secrets Manager.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Required on POST requests that create money-related records. Replays within 24 hours return the original response. Reuse with a different body returns 409 idempotency_conflict.

schema.description: Configured payment provider key. `fake` is the deterministic test provider, registered only outside prod (prod returns 404 for it).

OrgId.name: org_id
OrgId.description: Target organisation. Accepted only on /v1/platform endpoints.

InviteToken.name: token
InviteToken.description: The token from the set-password link.

Reason.name: reason
Reason.description: Why it is deleted. Kept in the audit log.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON, invalid or tampered cursor.

ValidationFailed.description: Request parsed but failed validation (code validation_error). `details` lists each failing field.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted for this role or resource (for example a tenant reading another tenant's lease).

NotFound.description: Resource not found in the caller's organisation. Resources belonging to other organisations are indistinguishable from missing ones.

Conflict.description: State conflict, duplicate or idempotency conflict. Domain codes include lease_overlap, invoice_already_exists, invalid_state, document_not_clean and idempotency_conflict.

Currency.description: ISO 4217. Only MYR in v1, modelled as a field so multi-currency can be added later.

amount_minor.description: Amount in minor units (sen). Never a float.

message.description: Human readable summary. Never contains personal data.

code.description: Machine-readable issue (0.16.0): the validator's error type, or a code made from the fixed English issue. Use it to show the issue in the user's language.

request_id.description: Correlation ID, also returned in the X-Request-Id header.

params.description: The values in `message`, for showing it in the user's language (e.g. `quota_exceeded`: `scope` (`plan`, `own`, `manager`), `limit`, `used`, `name`; `plan_read_only`: `date`, `until`; `address_suppressed`: `scope` (`tenant`, `staff`)). `message` stays the English fallback.

Role.description: `vendor` is reserved for a later release and is not issued in v1.

tenant_id.description: Set when the caller is a tenant.

active_from.description: Staff only: first day of access an admin set. Null: none.

active_until.description: Staff only: last day of access an admin set (inclusive). Null: no end date.

branding.description: The organisation's brand when branding is on.

percent_bp.description: Basis points of the overdue balance charged per whole month overdue (150 = 1.5%). Integer only: no floats anywhere in billing.

invoice_lead_days.description: Invoices are generated this many days before the due date.

reminder_offsets_days.description: Days relative to due date. Negative is before.

active_from.description: First day the account may be used (inclusive, Malaysian date). Null: no start limit.

active_until.description: Last day the account may be used (inclusive, Malaysian date). Null: no end date.

access.description: What the account allows today. `invited` and `active` can use the app; `scheduled` (before active_from), `expired` (after active_until) and `disabled` get 403 `account_inactive` at sign-in and on every request.

unit_quota.description: Property managers: most units at once in the properties they manage (whole units that are on; rooms and bays are free). Null: no limit of their own.

units_managed.description: Units (whole units that are on) in the properties they manage now.

active_until.description: Access ends after this date (inclusive). Must not be before active_from.

unit_quota.description: Units this property manager may have at once. The managers' limits together cannot exceed the organisation's plan (422).

active_from.description: Access starts on this date (inclusive). Explicit null removes the limit; omit to keep it.

active_until.description: Access ends after this date (inclusive). Must not be before active_from. Explicit null removes the limit; omit to keep it.

unit_quota.description: Units this property manager may have at once. The managers' limits together cannot exceed the organisation's plan (422).

status.description: `inactive`: deactivated, hidden from new leases (was `archived` before 0.9.0).

unit_count.description: Whole units, on or off. Rooms, parking bays and deleted units are not included.

units_active.description: Whole units that are on: what the plan and manager unit limits count (0.13.2). Sent by createProperty, getProperty and listProperties.

manager_id.description: The user who manages this property: its creator, reassignable by an org admin. A property manager sees only the properties they manage and what is attached to them.
Org admin only (403 otherwise): reassign to an active org admin or property manager of the organisation (422 otherwise).

parent_unit_id.description: Room: the whole unit it is in. Parking bay: the whole unit it is allocated to, or null for a property bay.
